key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking shifts from transgranular to intergranular as stress decreases, revealing the mechanism behind the brittle-to-ductile rupture transition.
engineering_relevance: The framework can help predict creep life and rupture mode in high-temperature alloys, supporting safer design against grain-boundary and grain-interior failure.
method: Explicit polycrystalline microstructure with crystal plasticity.
Coupled grain-boundary cavitation and crystallographic crack propagation.
Microscale simulations across different stress levels to map cracking transitions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microscale computations that reproduce stress-dependent cracking modes and link them to changes in rupture ductility and creep life.
watch_item: Model predictions depend on accurate calibration of grain-boundary cavitation and fracture parameters, so transferability to other alloys and loading conditions may require validation.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
